endorsements.quote: Our organization established a multidisciplinary clinical AI board to navigate the complexity associated with the incorporation of AI technology in the radiology department.
The AI board works in partnership with a patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) body.
This on-premises AI deployment engine, linked to the server, will enable performance assessment of AI software from a variety of vendors before clinical implementation in a “sandbox” environment.
An AI product that performs well on average may underperform in subgroups such as women, children, or ethnic minorities if these groups are underrepresented in training data.
Therefore, complementary prevalence-sensitive metrics such as area under the precision-recall curve and Brier scores should be utilized for robust evaluation.

For example, it assesses whether AI products meet applicable legal and regulatory requirements for medical devices (eg, holding a CE or UKCA mark and complying with the relevant UK medical device regulatory framework 16 ), AI research reporting guidelines (eg, TRIPOD-AI, 17 DECIDE-AI, 18 CONSORT-AI 19 ) and ethical principles.

unlisted_practices: Monitor deployed AI tools in real time for performance drift and calibration across patient subgroups, using a privacy-preserving monitoring service.
Use a structured scoring matrix to prioritize and appraise AI products, retaining the scores and rationale as institutional memory.
Select AI products with explainability features so clinicians can interrogate outputs to support informed decision-making and clear accountability.
Assess AI products' performance across demographic subgroups before deployment.
Build a secure on-premises sandbox infrastructure for benchmarking AI products from multiple vendors before clinical integration.

screen.reason: The paper outlines an institutional governance and implementation framework/strategy (AI board, sandbox, prioritization process) for radiology AI at a UK hospital, offering a pragmatic guide rather than reporting an empirical comparative study.
